headline: Gefitinib ranks 9 of 13 by pooled median binding pChEMBL on wild-type EGFR, and matched-assay results are mixed; no preclinical or clinical evidence has been retrieved.

sections.summary: Gefitinib has 30 comparable wild-type EGFR IC50 binding measurements, with a median pChEMBL of 7.69, placing it 9th of 13. Same-assay comparisons show it ahead of erlotinib or lapatinib in some assays and behind neratinib and others in other assays. Ranks pool different assays and labs and are indicative only. Mutant-variant measurements were excluded, so this ranking does not reflect activity in EGFR-mutant disease. Potency in binding assays does not establish clinical efficacy.

claims.text: Gefitinib: 30 comparable IC50 binding measurements on EGFR, median pChEMBL 7.69 (range 4.81–10), rank 9 of 13 by median.

Higher-ranked comparators by pooled median: mobocertinib (10.65, only 2 measurements, so uncertain), afatinib (8.86), neratinib (8.83), canertinib (8.77), icotinib (8.7), dacomitinib (8.16), pyrotinib (7.89) and lapatinib (7.87).
Lower-ranked comparators by pooled median: erlotinib (7.58), osimertinib (7.57), brigatinib (7.07) and rocilettinib (6.99).
Matched assay CHEMBL683041 (EGFR autophosphorylation): gefitinib pChEMBL 6.29 versus canertinib 7.13 (gefitinib weaker) and erlotinib 5.84 (gefitinib stronger).
Matched assay CHEMBL674106: gefitinib pChEMBL 9 versus lapatinib 8.
Matched assay CHEMBL892951 (1 uM ATP): gefitinib 8.27 versus neratinib 10.1. Matched assay CHEMBL892954 (1 mM ATP): gefitinib 5.56 versus neratinib 9.74, so the gap with neratinib widens at high ATP.
Matched assay CHEMBL924351: gefitinib 7.41 versus erlotinib 7.64. Matched assay CHEMBL944276: gefitinib 7.66 versus lapatinib 7.77. These differences are small.

sections.summary: No functional, cell-based or in vivo evidence was retrieved yet.
Clinical trial data was not yet retrieved for this report.
Computed properties only; these are calculated by ChEMBL and are not a safety assessment. No drug warnings were listed in the evidence.

claims.text: Computed properties for gefitinib: MW 446.91, AlogP 4.28, 0 Lipinski Ro5 violations, QED 0.52. These are not a safety assessment.

openQuestions: How does gefitinib compare with comparators against clinically relevant mutant EGFR (e.g. L858R, T790M), which were excluded from this ranking?
Do cell-based and in vivo data support the binding-assay picture?
Why does gefitinib's matched-assay potency drop at 1 mM ATP relative to 1 uM ATP?
What do human trials show for efficacy and safety in non-small cell lung cancer?
nextSteps: Retrieve and review clinical trial data for gefitinib in non-small cell lung cancer.
Add mutant-variant and cell-based potency data in a separate, labelled analysis.
Retrieve preclinical functional and in vivo evidence.
Check ChEMBL drug warnings and label safety data.
